gaps.hint: to his credit = in his favour
gaps.explanation: 'to somebody's credit' — something in their favour.
'beyond all expectations' = better than anyone predicted.

gaps.sentence: The two reports differ ___ several important respects.
___ any rate, we still have enough time.
gaps.explanation: 'At any rate' = whatever else is true.

gaps.sentence: The scheme paid off in the ___ — we recouped every euro.
He completed the marathon despite being ___ breath.
gaps.explanation: 'out of breath' = breathing fast from effort.

gaps.sentence: The smell was ___ this world — absolutely incredible.
He denied everything ___ the face of the evidence.
gaps.hint: ___ the face of = when confronted with
gaps.explanation: 'in the face of' = despite / when confronted by.
